Tiki Coconut Eggnog

Served at: Tiki Christmas at Pearl Harbor

Serves 6-8Prep 20 minCook 15 min

This tropical twist on classic eggnog brings the festive spirit of a Hawaiian Christmas right to your glass. Creamy, rich, and infused with the exotic flavor of coconut, it's the perfect cooling yet warming beverage to celebrate a 'Tiki Christmas at Pearl Harbor,' blending traditional holiday cheer with island paradise vibes.

Ingredients

  • 6 large egg yolks
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 (13.5 oz / 400 ml) can full-fat coconut milk
  • 1 cup (240 ml) heavy cream
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, plus more for garnish
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon (optional)
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1 cup (240 ml) dark rum, or to taste

Method

  1. In a medium heatproof bowl, whisk the egg yolks and granulated sugar together until the mixture is pale yellow and creamy.
  2. In a medium saucepan, combine the full-fat coconut milk, heavy cream, 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, and optional cinnamon. Heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the mixture is simmering gently around the edges but not boiling.
  3. Slowly temper the egg mixture: gradually whisk about 1 cup (240 ml) of the hot coconut milk mixture into the egg yolks, whisking constantly to prevent the eggs from scrambling.
  4. Pour the tempered egg mixture back into the saucepan with the remaining hot coconut milk mixture.
  5. Cook over low to medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or heatproof spatula, until the mixture thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon (about 8-12 minutes). Do not let it boil.
  6. Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in the vanilla extract.
  7. Pour the eggnog through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl or pitcher to ensure a smooth consistency.
  8. Cover the eggnog and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until it is thoroughly chilled.
  9. Just before serving, stir in the dark rum. Taste and adjust the amount of rum if desired.
  10. Serve the chilled coconut eggnog in festive glasses, garnished with a sprinkle of fresh nutmeg or a tropical touch like a pineapple wedge or toasted coconut flakes.

Tips

  • For a non-alcoholic version, simply omit the rum and add a splash of coconut extract for extra flavor.
  • To achieve an extra frothy texture, you can whisk the eggnog vigorously just before serving, or top each glass with a dollop of whipped cream.
  • For an authentic Tiki presentation, garnish with a small paper umbrella or a maraschino cherry.
